name: creation

attributes.attribute: towed land with a straw rope that broke
stranded island left in the sea
struck an escaping bull with a rod
old woman with a blue-gray face and one eye

sources: Monaghan, Patricia. The Encyclopedia of Celtic Mythology and Folklore. Checkmark Books, 2008.
text: The oldest gods of a region draw to themselves the tales of creation. People settled Ireland before the Celts came, about seven thousand years earlier. The Cailleach made the islands that lie off Munster, in the southwestern corner of Ireland. She towed land on a straw rope. The rope snapped, and the two isles of Scariff and Deenish came to rest apart in the sea. Another tale says she hit a fleeing bull with a rod while he swam away from her. The bull became an island of rock. People painted the Cailleach as an aged woman whose skin carried a faint blue-gray tone. Her eyesight was uncannily sharp. She could make out an object twenty miles off no worse than her own hand, though she had one eye. She had great strength for her age. Her strength let her beat any reaper in the land when they met head to head. Her look was unappealing.

okr.objective: Creation legends attach to the oldest divinities, such as the Cailleach.
key_results: The Cailleach formed the islands off Munster by towing land on a straw rope.
The rope broke and left Scariff and Deenish stranded in the sea.
She struck an escaping bull with a rod and turned it into rock.
She had a blue-gray face, one eye, and eyesight sharp enough to see twenty miles.
okr.evidence: Monaghan, Encyclopedia of Celtic Mythology and Folklore
